<a id="beach_flick"></a>
## The Ride of the Valkyries as Surf Rock: `beach_flick.yml`

Beach flick: the Ride of the Valkyries as sixties surf rock, after Misirlou (Dick Dale and His Del-
Tones). The horn theme of the Ride of the Valkyries (Richard Wagner, 1856) is public domain and is
played as written, in its key and its nine-eight time, from Claude's knowledge of the score; the
tremolo picking is how the guitar plays it, and the runs with their flat seconds, the trumpet's
answers, the solos and the drums are new, with nothing of the reference's own tune quoted.

<a id="magic_colored_smoke"></a>
## The Ride of the Valkyries as Psychedelic Rock: `magic_colored_smoke.yml`

Magic colored smoke: the Ride of the Valkyries as sixties psychedelic rock for a trio and an organ,
after Purple Haze (the Jimi Hendrix Experience). The horn theme of the Ride of the Valkyries
(Richard Wagner, 1856) is public domain and is played as written, in its key and its nine-eight
time, from Claude's knowledge of the score; the heavy bass figure, the bent licks with their flat
fifths, the solos and the loose drums are new, and nothing of the reference's own riff is quoted.

<a id="night_on_the_moog"></a>
## Night on Bald Mountain as Horror-Film Progressive Rock: `night_on_the_moog.yml`

Night on the Moog: Night on Bald Mountain as the progressive rock of seventies Italian horror films.
The creeping bass figure and the low brass theme of Night on Bald Mountain (Modest Mussorgsky, 1867,
as Rimsky-Korsakov arranged it) are public domain and are played as written, read from the Mutopia
Project's piano edition; the synthesizer bass, the bells' arpeggios, the choir, the licks, the solos
and the drums are new.

<a id="three_chord_joy"></a>
## The Ode to Joy as Punk Rock: `three_chord_joy.yml`

Three chord joy: the Ode to Joy as seventies punk rock. The tune of the Ode to Joy from the Ninth
Symphony (Ludwig van Beethoven, 1824) is public domain and is played as written, from Claude's
knowledge of the score; the downstroked chords, the octave licks, the solos and the drums are new.

<a id="turkish_surf"></a>
## The Rondo alla Turca as Surf Rock: `turkish_surf.yml`

Turkish surf: the Rondo alla Turca as sixties surf rock. The opening theme and the middle theme of
the Rondo alla Turca from the Piano Sonata No. 11 (Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, about 1783) are public
domain and are played as written, an octave down on the guitar, from Claude's knowledge of the
score; the runs with their flat seconds, the saxophone's answers, the solos and the drums are new.
